English: Brush Fence
A simple, quickly-woven brush fence marks the first boundary of the settlement, offering minimal deterrence to intruders but helping define the clans territory.
Earthen Bank
A low embankment of piled earth and sod, reinforcing the outer boundary and providing a modicum of defense for the camp.
Wooden Palisade
Stout timber stakes form a palisade, greatly increasing the defensive value of the ringfort and deterring would-be raiders.
Stone Guard Hut
A fortified stone hut is erected near the entrance, serving as a watch post and a symbol of increasing permanence.
Inner Ditch
A deep and broad ditch dug on the inner side of the palisade, hindering attackers and improving the forts resilience.
Outer Rampart
A second, higher rampart of earth and stone, encircling the original defenses and greatly enhancing the strongholds security.
Gatehouse Pavilion
A timber and stone gatehouse, manned at all hours and offering a defensible point of entry and exit for the fort.
Defended Roundhouse
A large, centrally-located roundhouse with thick wattle-and-daub walls, serving as both a command center and a last redoubt for the clans elite.
Chiefs Ring
A sacred inner ring reserved for the chieftains family and council, adorned with ritual stones and guarded by loyal retainers. The heart of the clans unity and strength.
High Ringfort
An imposing, multi-ringed stronghold with massive ramparts, stone towers, and sacred enclosures. The ultimate symbol of clan might and security, drawing kin and followers from afar.
